sections.label: NEXT ACTION
sections.bodyHtml: Continue bright light without harsh sudden sun; keep each small pot lightly moist while rooting, but not waterlogged. Check each cutting individually for firm stems, new leafy shoots, and eventual root establishment. No need to pinch newly establishing plants yet.

sections.label: CURRENT CONDITION
sections.bodyHtml: Owner reports 17 separate clones propagated from Jango. Three chat photographs on Nov 4 show several small individual pots containing green, upright Pelargonium cuttings with lobed green leaves and many small growing points. Growth and leaf posture look encouraging overall, with varying stem lengths and foliage density. Root development and survival of every one of the 17 are not independently verified.

sections.label: PARENT PLANT
sections.bodyHtml: Jango (GAIA #45), scented geranium / citronella-type Pelargonium. These are vegetative clones of the original plant, kept together as one group catalog entry rather than 17 separate GAIA cards.

sections.label: CLONE ROSTER
sections.bodyHtml:
Proposed Star Wars names (17): Rex · Cody · Fives · Echo · Jesse · Kix · Tup · Hardcase · Wolffe · Gregor · Hunter · Wrecker · Tech · Crosshair · Omega · Boba · 99.
These names are a shared roster only; individual name-to-pot assignments have not yet been identified or confirmed.

sections.label: WATER
sections.bodyHtml: For unrooted or recently rooted cuttings, keep the mix lightly and evenly moist while allowing excess to drain; avoid standing water in trays. Once roots are established and growth is steady, allow the upper part of the mix to dry between thorough waterings. Check each pot, since drying speeds can vary.

sections.label: LIGHT
sections.bodyHtml: Bright indirect light or adequate grow lights while establishing. After rooting, acclimate gradually to stronger light to encourage compact foliage and shorter internodes.

sections.label: FERTILIZER
sections.bodyHtml: Wait until rooting and sustained new growth are evident. Thereafter feed lightly with a balanced fertilizer during active growth, following label guidance.

sections.label: LOCATION
sections.bodyHtml: Small grouped pots pictured on metal grow-light shelves; exact permanent location and light distance not recorded.

sections.label: REPOT
sections.bodyHtml: Do not immediately move cuttings into oversized pots. Wait until each rooted cutting has a working root system and needs more space; pot up gradually.

sections.label: SOIL
sections.bodyHtml: Photos show small pots with an airy, perlite-containing mix; exact composition and drainage remain unverified. Prefer lightly moisture-retentive but freely draining potting mix.

sections.label: WATCH
sections.bodyHtml: Monitor new leaves, expanding branching, wilt or dark/soft stems, and whether the soil stays too wet. A few pots show pale specks on the surface that may be perlite or other substrate material; identify by close inspection rather than assuming pests or mold. Track rooting by pot when possible.

sections.label: FUTURE SHAPING
sections.bodyHtml: Once well rooted and growing strongly, pinch a small terminal growing tip just above a node if you want bushier clones. Keep enough green leaf area, and root healthy tip cuttings to expand the group further.

sections.label: KEEPERS & GIFTS
sections.bodyHtml: Owner plans to give away most of the 17 Jango cuttings once they are well established, keeping Boba for certain and possibly one other clone. No specific pot has been assigned to Boba yet, and no plants have been given away. Revisit selection and labels once rooting and growth are established.
